clues.title: Plate: Vibes
text: If you see a license plate with a blue strip while driving left with this climate/landscape, you know you're in Malta. If you can't see the driving direction, use other clues like limestone rock walls to recognize Malta.

clues.title: Landscape: Vibes
text: The general landscape of Malta consists of slightly hilly dry agricultural fields. Many roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide, due to the island’s size. Having a mediterranean climate, cacti and various dry shrubs can be seen.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

text: Malta drives on the left.

clues.title: Rock Walls

This alone is usually enough to determine that you are in Malta.

clues.title: Street sign: Triq
text: The Maltese word for street is “triq”, which can be seen on almost every street sign.

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture

Buildings made of limestone are also fairly common.

clues.title: Plate: Malta
text: Like most of Europe, Maltese licence plates have a blue strip on the left. However, unlike most of Europe, short plates are very common.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Language: Maltese
text: While English is the primary language of Malta, it is also common to see the Maltese language. Maltese is a Semitic language sharing its origin with Arabic, but written with the Latin script and heavily influenced by Italian. Unique letters for Maltese include **Ċ, Ġ, Ż** and **Ħ**.
The Maltese word for street is **triq**, which can be seen on almost every street sign in Malta.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
